metadata.description: The world cut from layered paper under a desk lamp up and to the left: the water in five teal sheets stepping down from every shore to an ink floor, each sheet's edge where a depth field (the land blurred away from the shore, near and far) crosses a cut-off, wobbled as if cut by hand; the land the top sheet, oatmeal with a deckled lit edge, a thick cut face and the longest shadow, its piers merged from afar, its uses (homes, shops, works, institutions) thin sheets of their own stock on it, and its streets carved in as grooves, a narrow shadowed wall on one side and a lit one on the other, deeper for the major roads; thinner sage parks glued on it, card bridges over the water, ferries stitched across it in one thread that fades toward the far side of the view, the landmark a card star, and up close the buildings as card stacked one, two or three sheets thick by height, kraft, cream and white; every sheet with a lit edge, a cut face and a crisp shadow down and to the right; one paper stock throughout, its grain softer from afar
